how: The room recruited members to draw the mascot and renewed appeals when competitors took over.
Members answered the drawing call with bare commitments to join.
The starter explicitly attributed difficulty keeping the sprite whole to rival scripts and too few participants.
Explaining the half-mascot to an outsider during ongoing defence is now covered without requiring a finished picture.
A participant reports stopping without identifying stress, criticism, or an internal quarrel as the reason.
The starter proposed the image and supplied its location, while ensuing joins remain separate acceptance actions.
The proposed image represented the fandom through a character explicitly described as its half-mascot.
Members announced resumed work and reported missing or overwritten features of the developing image.
Coordinates, reference images, and an answered colour question made the shared drawing actionable.
A reference already in circulation was clarified by an explicit colour question and correction.
The room distributed browser-console instructions and later explicitly reported trying to defend with scripts.
Participation instructions distinguished computer and mobile devices without establishing any individual time cost or personal hardship.
Browser and app instructions do not report site faults, timer anomalies, or tests of extra pixels.
Discord-hosted images and proposed contact with another community do not establish moving the room's planning into a chat.
Private requests to stop or move do not establish concealed strategy or infiltration of rival venues.
One room cannot test cross-room prevalence, and public instructions do not determine whether formal authority existed elsewhere.
Core defence operates here, while the revised claim about reversing agreed changes remains untested by the colour correction.
A participant tentatively identified the encroaching logo and suggested contacting the implicated community.
The initial anchor coordinates instantiate choosing a location, while subsequent loss-driven moves require the separate relocation process.
After the first spot became inhospitable, the starter sought another location and announced renewed work at different coordinates.
Participants proposed negotiation, shared space, limits on expansion, and rebuilding terms with neighbours.
A neighbour's warning about overlap received an explicit promise not to cover the flag.
A neighbour's warning elicited a restraint promise before a previously settled border was demonstrated.
Incoming proposals offered shared space or rebuilding help, and one reported offer received explicit acceptance.
Distinguish proposed help and accepted terms from evidence that the promised placements were delivered.
Alliance openness and acceptance of rebuilding terms do not document an operating coalition or completed joint defence.
A participant reported speaking to another community and relayed its willingness to ally.
A member explicitly withheld a side because they were both a Red Wings fan and a Kamen Rider fan.
Shared-space and relocation proposals do not show a host exercising rule over guests.
The offer and assent disclose neither a dispute over binding members nor a disclaimer of the speaker's standing.
Calling rivals bullies and promising restraint do not by themselves establish an exchange debating whether covering work is fair.
The room carried fandom lore into its half-mascot explanation and Mighty Action rally.
A member's dual fandom does not establish a pre-existing quarrel carried into the canvas.
The cited threats concern contested pixels and rival scripts without an inherited rivalry named as the reason to attack.
Familiar fandom and game phrases do not establish creating a new collective joke about the canvas work.
Invoking an existing fandom's half-mascot does not document forming a new canvas room.
The coded hostile language is not accompanied by an argument about slurs, offensive jokes, or hate symbols.
Members recognised the Strega rumor as an April Fools joke and mocked the suggestion that anyone believed it.
Treat prank recognition as reception unless evidence identifies the room as its producer or connects it to the canvas call.
A prank reveal prompted interest in its underlying character, distinct from testing the rumor or explaining the canvas.
The coded moderator instructions organise placement without documenting a posting boundary or rule containing canvas talk.
Coded hostility concerns neighbours rather than members sabotaging their own mark because of unwanted canvas posts.
Members praised everyone's work and the honour of placing together despite acknowledging the missed goal.
Members marked Game Over, linked a final snapshot, and remembered the remnant of the first drawing.
A visitor title and subsequent mascot explanation do not reveal whether canvas visibility caused arrival or recruited ordinary participation.
Explaining the mascot to a visitor does not establish seeking notice from creators, the team, or the press.
Appreciating the surviving fragment does not document carrying the project into another canvas, organisation, or enduring relationship.
The snapshot and remnant appreciation do not contest another version, correct an account, or request cleanup.
A greeting with a removed request supports contact alone unless surviving evidence specifies the help sought or offered.
An incoming proposal called for jointly displacing rival builders, without demonstrating an executed raid.
Participants cursed named rivals while helping and after the canvas closed.
Recruitment, joins, and later reports establish a sequence without measuring the call's effect on actual building.
When the proposal itself calls members to participate, proposing and recruitment need not be separate ordered events.
Placed features became objects of defence while completion of the whole image remained uncertain.
Participants explicitly coupled takeover reports with proposals to negotiate or seek rebuilding partners.
A direct warning and restraint promise do not establish an already settled border governing subsequent pixel compliance.
The last-stand post explicitly presents a newly found script as a response to rival takeovers.
Automation can remain insufficient when rival scripts operate and members still judge their participation inadequate.
Explaining praise must allow valued participation and a surviving feature as grounds despite explicit failure to complete the goal.
Praise and the final snapshot coexist without a cited reply linking praise to the decision to preserve an image.
The final record does not disclose a subsequent decision to reuse the work or retain a canvas-created organisation.
Scarce hands can coexist with continuing defence and alliance seeking rather than selecting abandonment or relocation.
The reference precedes a colour correction without evidence that template publication settled a prior design debate.
A direct reply accepts the starter's drawing call with an unqualified commitment to join.
Written acceptance supports the observed commitment but cannot determine silent placement or the form of unobserved refusals.
Strain and help offers are documented, but arrival of the promised external help remains unverified.
Negotiating and accepting rebuilding terms is an intermediate outcome before help delivery can be established.
Space-for-help terms demonstrate proposed reciprocity without verifying that border talk produced an executed exchange.
Recruitment and adversarial proposals are visible without showing that the call redirected placers from building to attack.
The flag complaint and restraint promise do not answer the adversarial proposal and cannot establish its refusal mechanism.
Negotiation and adversarial proposals coexist without a cited answer invoking a truce to reject an attack call.
The later curse does not explicitly answer or recall the earlier proposal to displace rivals.
Alliance openness under strain does not establish coalition formation and joint defence.
Recruitment is visible without a coded posting flood producing a moderation boundary.
The offer and acceptance show neither a later refusal to be bound nor a limit stated while terms were made.
Relocation renewed coordination through a different location, sprite references, and an ensuing colour question.
